basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 10.' and it opens 'VERS. 10.-- Et fluvius egrediebatur de loco voluptatis ad irrigandum paradisum, qui inde'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 10.-- Et fluvius egrediebatur de loco voluptatis ad irrigandum paradisum, qui inde dividitur in quatuor capita. Sciendum est quia nec per hoc paradisus | disus declaratur evidenter ubi sit, quasi per flumina inveniri possit locus ipsius. Qui sicuti nonnulli dicunt, et beatus Augustinus autumat, licet ab uno fonte Scriptura teste procedant, tamen subtus terra profluunt, et post longos tractus suis locis erumpunt et celantur interim amnes.
